decisions.decision: Severe-latency reclassification is gated on measured THROUGHPUT, not latency alone
decisions.rationale: iOS has NO public API for signal strength. A slow probe could legitimately be weak signal rather than a modem defect, and blaming the modem for bad coverage would be dishonest and would let Apple tear the dataset apart. Weak signal degrades latency AND throughput together (physics); a modem stall gives bad latency with HEALTHY throughput. Four branches: slow+healthy -> DROP; slow+poor -> not a drop; slow+no/stale data -> not a drop (conservative); fast -> clean.

decisions.decision: Private APIs for signal strength (CTGetSignalStrength, status-bar scraping) are REJECTED
decisions.rationale: They would work on a sideloaded build, but a diagnostic tool that reads undocumented internals hands Apple a free way to dismiss the entire dataset. The export is evidence in a live escalation.

decisions.decision: Historical events are NEVER retroactively reclassified
decisions.rationale: The 100+ days in the store are evidence. Events from June have no referenceThroughputKbps and cannot be honestly reclassified. The new rule applies going forward only, and the report says so.

decisions.decision: Stop pursuing a hardware replacement / ERS
decisions.rationale: Three phone swaps reproduced the fault because EVERY iPhone would. A like-for-like replacement fixes nothing and accepting one as closure ends the case. Ersatzlieferung is therefore a worthless remedy; only a software fix or Wandelung (refund) actually helps.

decisions.decision: Tell Apple about the Tello finding rather than concealing it; reframe as 'I have isolated a deterministic reproduction'
decisions.rationale: The sysdiagnose already contains the second eSIM in plain sight — concealment is impossible and would destroy credibility, which is the main asset in a goodwill negotiation. A deterministic repro is worth more to Engineering than 317 drop logs.

decisions.decision: Wi-Fi Calling was a BAD recommendation and was corrected
decisions.rationale: User correctly refuted it: with no Wi-Fi in range (i.e. exactly when the problem occurs, out on cellular) the line still has to hunt. Correct model: MANUAL NETWORK SELECTION is what stops the hunt (3GPP: automatic mode = continuous full-band PLMN search; manual mode = attempt one PLMN, fail, stop). Wi-Fi Calling is only a reachability BACKSTOP after the cellular registration is dead.

context_notes: THIS SESSION STOPPED BEING APP DEVELOPMENT AND BECAME A FIELD INVESTIGATION. CellGuard is now instrumentation for a live Apple escalation and a possible Swiss consumer-law claim. Data integrity is paramount — a SwiftData migration crash would destroy 100+ days of irreplaceable evidence, which is why both new @Model properties this session are optional. ROOT CAUSE (settled, do not re-litigate): the second eSIM (Tello, US voice-only) cannot register on any Swiss network, so it searches continuously. iPhone is DSDS — both lines share ONE RF chain — and paging/signalling/network-search on the idle line outranks packet data on the active line. The Swisscom line therefore reports full bars + 5G while passing zero data for hours, and iOS never detects it. CONFIRMED BY APPLE'S OWN TELEMETRY: Settings -> Battery -> 'Poor Cell Coverage' shows ~zero on exactly the two days Tello was off (Wed 7/8, Fri 7/10, dates VERIFIED) and 1.5-3.5% on every other day. RULED OUT: region locale (user set region back to US, issue did not return — the 2026-07-08 'region=CH is the fix' conclusion was WRONG); 5G SA hunting (failure occurs on 5G AND LTE, so RAT preference is not the variable). EXPERIMENT RUNNING since 2026-07-11: Tello line ON, Network Selection -> Manual -> Sunrise, showing ZERO BARS (confirmed = did not register = the intended test). PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS: (1) Poor Cell Coverage stays ~0 with the line ON -> manual mode killed the hunt -> iOS had a remedy available all along and neither applied nor surfaced it (devastating for Apple); (2) Poor Cell Coverage returns to 1.5-3.5% -> iOS silently ignored manual selection and fell back to automatic scanning (a defect in its own right). UNEXPLAINED, worth chasing: the three multi-hour 'zombie modem' events all start at 04:49 / 04:55 / 05:09 — same time of day. A ~24h retry timer (3GPP T3245, the forbidden-PLMN retry timer, max 24h) would produce exactly this. Present to Apple as a hypothesis for THEM to test, not as a conclusion. Full narrative is in .planning/STATE.md ('ROOT CAUSE FOUND' block) and in Claude's memory file project_connectivity_root_causes.md.
